newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Cullen won't return until fully fit.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Cullen won't return until fully fit.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Feb 7 - All Black fullback Christian Cullen won't be returning to the rugby field until he is 100 percent fit, NZPA reports.
However, his injured knee, from which a cartilage was removed before Christmas, is improving.
"It is getting there," said Cullen. "I had a run, a light 30-minute jog, for the first time on Monday; so that's a positive sign."

He had expected to be back jogging after two to three weeks but his operation had proved "a bit more serious" than expected so doctors advised him to wait the standard six weeks for a cartilage removal.
"I have also been given the message by John Hart and the selectors not to go out if I'm not 100 percent, even if it does mean missing a few Super 12 games."
Cullen would love to play the Super 12 opener between his Hurricanes and the Waikato Chiefs in Palmerston North where he now lives.
"But if I'm not 100, I'm not going to push it," he says.

He won't be playing for the Hurricanes at the Adelaide Sevens and the Ballymore 10s. But he would contemplate 20 to 30 minutes against Queensland Country at Toowoomba on February 18 if the knee responds over the next week.
He has been told to always expect the knee to be a little sore after running on it.
"Walking around sometimes it locks up and I have to get it mobilised by the physio," he said.
He said when he turned up to the All Black camp recently, he was at least relieved to see other players with niggling injuries, besides himself.
And his fitness shouldn't have suffered greatly because he has been active in the gym and with swimming and cycling.

It is just frustrating for Cullen, he admits, to reflect on how the injury happened -- when he went for a high ball in the test at Johannesburg and thudded into the Ellis Park turf without an opponent laying a hand on him.
